profile.what: Two-sided B2B travel distribution platform (TBO.com): ~1 million+ hotels and 750+ airlines (AR FY25 figures quoted in the Jun-2026 deck) sold to ~159,000 travel buyers (retail travel agents, tour operators, OTAs, TMCs, loyalty programmes) in 100+ countries. Among the top 4 B2B travel distribution platforms globally (company).
products: Air tickets, mostly sold by Indian agents (93% of air GTV is India-sourced in FY26). Low take rate (~2.2-2.6% of GTV) and GP ~1.2% of GTV: a traffic and cross-sell engine
Hotels, transfers, car rental, cruises, rail, insurance; ~64% of FY26 GTV and ~87% of organic GP. International source markets (Europe, MEA, APAC, LATAM, North America) are ~60% of organic GTV
US B2B2C luxury travel company serving ~10,000 high-end travel advisors; acquired 1-Oct-2025 for USD 125 mn; revenue recognised on check-in; take rate ~25% of GTV, GP ~13% of GTV
TBO Academy, white-label and technical services
profile.model: Revenue is recognised net (commission/markup) for most bookings; GP = revenue less service fees (payment to suppliers/partners where revenue is gross). Most profit is booked in Tek Travels DMCC/FZCO (Dubai), the holding company for the international business.
profile.subsidiaries: Tek Travels DMCC (Dubai), BookaBed AG, Jumbonline (Spain), Island Holidays, United Experts (Saudi), TBO LLC and Classic Vacations LLC (US), TBO Tek Ireland, Australia, Indonesia, Greece, Israel, Poland

guidance: Aim for both QoQ and YoY growth; Q2 'somewhat better than Q1' (July is the peak northern-hemisphere month); once the Middle East normalises, organic growth returns to the Q3FY26 profile (Jan-Feb 2026 organic growth was 'far higher than 15%'). Strategy: 'upwards of 20%' topline growth plus margin expansion
Organic SG&A grew 4% in constant currency in Q1; may expand 'a little' (increments in Q2, opportunistic market development) but 'not at the pace of top line'; hosting cost cut is the new baseline

Tracks EBITDA/GP (organic 27.5% in Q1 vs 23.5% in Q4FY26), which should keep improving; no margin guidance; scaled peers (Hotelbeds, WebBeds) run 45-60% EBITDA/GP 'which we are not at all anchoring towards'
Full-year EBITDA ~2.5% of GTV is 'a fair assessment' (3.4% in peak Q1); Q2 is CV's weakest quarter; platform migration by end-CY2026; cost synergies largely in the numbers, revenue synergies to come
H&A GP/GTV fell to 5.2% (organic) in Q1 from 5.5% in Q4FY26 (Middle East mix and price cuts to hold volume); expected to gravitate to the historical average in the near term
Acquisition loan: 5 years, 1-year moratorium, repayment from Q3FY27 over four years
history: Founded by Ankush Nijhawan and Gaurav Bhatnagar in Delhi (Travel Boutique Online)
International operations begin in the UAE; Naspers acquires a stake (2012), later sold
Brazil operations (2015); first acquisition Island Hopper; USD 1 bn GTV milestone; Affirma Capital (ex-Standard Chartered PE) invests
Acquires Bookabed AG (2022) and Jumbonline (Spain, 2023); General Atlantic buys a minority stake from Affirma entities (announced 22-Oct-2023)
IPO at Rs920 (fresh Rs400 cr, OFS Rs1,151 cr); listed 15-May-2024
Acquires Classic Vacations (USA) for USD 125 mn; consolidated from 1-Oct-2025
Middle East conflict disrupts Gulf hubs and East-West travel; rupee depreciation inflates INR growth (11-point gap on hotel GTV in Q1FY27)
